_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 22:14:25Z)**_

The short answer: DeadReckon has built much of the hard execution kernel, but it has not yet delivered the complete original experience.

Today it is a serious local verified-run system. It is not yet a dependable “start this goal, walk away, and trust it to keep working until the goal is genuinely complete” product.

## Where the project stands

| Original promise | Current state | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Define “done” before starting | Plain English can be compiled into `acceptance.yaml`; an LLM critic looks for weak checks and goals a stub could satisfy | Strong, although users can still fall back to detected project tests instead of consciously approving a real contract |
| Run coding CLIs in isolation | Git worktree and copy isolation are mature; changes require deliberate promotion | Strong for source isolation |
| Keep running until the goal is met | A normal run is foreground and limited to 12 turns; recovery normally requires `resume`. Chain has detached execution; current uncommitted plan work adds orphan adoption | Major remaining gap |
| Independently judge completion | A separate gate runs deterministic checks and validates the completion marker | Strong deterministic floor, but not the semantic meta-judge described in the original vision |
| Resist a dishonest worker | The worker cannot bypass a failing test merely by claiming completion; tamper checks catch several forms of weakening | Useful protection, but current “cannot forge” language overstates the boundary |
| Capture the whole run | State, snapshots, events, traces, spend, provenance, implementation notes and reports are persisted | One of the strongest parts of the system |
| Make the experience pleasant | The default five-command interface is quite good | Internally, too many execution models and advanced commands still leak into the mental model |

The most important correction is about the judge. The LLM currently helps write and critique the definition of done in [acceptance.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/acceptance.rs:642). Final acceptance is then deterministic. There is no independent LLM reading the original goal, the resulting change and the evidence and deciding whether the goal was semantically achieved.

That means the original `/goal` idea is only partly present: semantic judgment happens before execution, not at the final boundary.

The current run loop also has a real ceiling: normal runs configure 12 turns in [run.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:496), after which the loop fails with a budget-exhausted state. State is durable, but the worker is not automatically durable. If its supervising process disappears, the job waits for an operator to resume or adopt it.

## What has genuinely been achieved

DeadReckon now has a credible “verified run” primitive:

1. Create an isolated workspace.
2. establish a completion contract;
3. run a chosen coding CLI;
4. retain state and evidence after every turn;
5. respond to gate failures with another corrective turn;
6. accept only after the external gate passes;
7. deliberately promote or export the result.

That is substantial. The current working tree passed the complete workspace test suite: 2,049 tests passed and none failed. I did not modify the repository.

The evidence system is also unusually thorough. [RunView](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/run_view.rs:20) gives a useful read model over persisted state and ledgers. The promotion boundary in [promotion.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:25) makes “completed” meaningfully different from “applied to my repository.”

So this is not a speculative pile of commands. It contains a real, tested kernel.

## Necessary complexity

These are inherent to the product and should remain:

- Safely isolating and later promoting source changes.
- Supporting different CLI providers and their different streaming, cancellation and accounting behaviour.
- Durable job identity, state, locking, recovery and cancellation.
- Compiling acceptance criteria into executable checks.
- A semantic judge for requirements that cannot be reduced to tests.
- Preventing the worker from modifying its own acceptance mechanism.
- Recording enough evidence to explain why a result was accepted.
- Scheduling dependent and parallel units of verified work.
- Explicit budgets, deadlines and blocked states. “Until done” must not mean “loop forever.”

## Incidental complexity

This is complexity created by the current shape of the implementation rather than the underlying problem:

- Forty-five top-level command variants, even though most are hidden from ordinary help.
- Several overlapping journey concepts: run, chain, plan/fork/merge, campaign, reshape and others.
- Control truth spread across state JSON, several JSONL ledgers and sidecar files, requiring hand-written reconciliation and orphan adoption.
- Repeated provider, retry, narration and budget policies in different orchestration layers.
- Multiple documentation and narration pipelines.
- Compatibility aliases, no-op flags and old spellings.
- Making implementation-note production part of the completion ritual, rather than deriving the after-state account from captured evidence.
- Continuing to deepen campaigns, learning, narration and other secondary systems before unattended goal execution is fully dependable.

The architectural smell is: there is one good verified-run atom, but too many ways to arrange and supervise it.

## The trust-boundary problem

The README’s “it can’t fake the finish” claim is stronger than the current implementation warrants.

The gate nonce is stored inside the run directory, and the marker uses Rust’s `DefaultHasher` in [gate.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:752), rather than a cryptographic MAC or signature. General CLI-provider and Bash-tool execution do not consistently deny access to gate material. In addition, automatic sandbox selection can fall back to no sandbox.

The system can truthfully say:

> A separate process runs the acceptance checks, and an existing completion marker cannot make failing checks pass.

It cannot yet universally say:

> A hostile coding agent is technically unable to forge acceptance.

Results should distinguish:

- `VERIFIED + CONFINED`
- `VERIFIED + UNCONFINED`
- `NEEDS REVIEW`
- `FAILED`

That would make the confidence claim precise rather than absolute.

## Where I would take it next

### 1. Finish the durable goal executor

Make `deadreckon start` create a durable local job, return its ID and detach by default. A small supervisor or user service should:

- lease pending jobs;
- recover abandoned leases;
- restart after terminal or machine failure;
- retain bounded retry, spend and time policies;
- distinguish blocked, cancelled, budget-exhausted and failed;
- supervise runs, chains and plans through the same scheduler.

Temporal is the useful exemplar here. Its core model is a durable execution reconstructed from an append-only event history, with explicit lifecycle operations such as start, describe, result, cancel, terminate and reset. DeadReckon should extract those durability and operator-semantics patterns without becoming a distributed workflow platform. [Temporal workflow execution](https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution), [Temporal CLI workflow commands](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/command-reference/workflow).

### 2. Restore the semantic meta-judge as a second key

Completion should require:

1. Deterministic checks pass.
2. An independent, read-only semantic judge assesses the goal, contract, diff and evidence.

The semantic judge must never override failed deterministic checks. It should return `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`, with evidence-backed reasons. If it is unavailable in strict mode, the result becomes `NEEDS REVIEW`, not accepted.

This is necessary complexity: natural-language goals cannot always be completely compiled into tests.

### 3. Close the gate boundary

- Keep signing material outside the agent-visible workspace.
- Use HMAC-SHA-256 or a proper signature.
- Deny gate and proof paths across every provider and tool route.
- Bind the receipt to the contract, policy, source revision and resulting revision.
- Fail closed for unattended trusted runs.
- Add adversarial tests in which an agent deliberately searches for and attempts to forge the marker.

### 4. Collapse the product around one job model

Keep the ordinary surface:

```text
start
attach
status
list
finish
```

Plans, chains and campaigns should become internal scheduling shapes or an explicitly advanced namespace. They should all create the same durable jobs and verified-run receipts.

Similarly, create one append-only control event history and derive current state and `RunView` from it. Rich spend, trace and documentation evidence can remain separate, but lifecycle truth should have one source.

### 5. Freeze secondary expansion and dogfood the promise

Temporarily freeze deeper campaign features, learning/improve surfaces and additional narration variants. Test the core promise on 20–30 real tasks across multiple repositories and providers.

Measure:

- unattended verified completion rate;
- automatic recovery rate;
- false acceptance and false rejection;
- number of operator interventions;
- time required to understand the final result;
- supervision and judging cost.

Kill the terminal, worker and machine during these trials. Remove network access. Attempt to tamper with the gate. Run DeadReckon on DeadReckon itself.

## Bottom line

DeadReckon contains a strong, unusually well-tested verified-run kernel inside an overgrown product.

The next phase should not be more orchestration features. It should make one promise completely true:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

Once that experience is reliable and pleasant, the plans, chains and campaigns become valuable multipliers instead of competing product models.

I’ll unpack “finish the durable goal executor” in concrete DeadReckon terms: what it means, what changes for the user, and what it does not require. I’m using the teaching skill because this is an architectural concept tied directly to this workspace.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 22:14:25Z)**_

“Finish the durable goal executor” means making DeadReckon responsible for the job after the user starts it.

Right now, DeadReckon has durable records, but not fully durable execution.

## Today

A normal run behaves roughly like this:

```text
Your terminal
    ↓
deadreckon run
    ↓
coding CLI
    ↓
gate
```

The `deadreckon run` process is the supervisor. While that process is alive, it keeps giving the coding CLI turns and checking the result.

DeadReckon saves enough state to recover, but:

- closing the supervisor stops the work;
- restarting the computer stops the work;
- someone must run `resume`;
- a normal attempt stops after 12 turns;
- detached execution exists for chains, but is not the common execution model.

That is resumable execution: “we can pick up where we stopped.”

It is not yet durable execution: “DeadReckon continues to own the job until it reaches a legitimate stopping point.”

## The proposed experience

The user should be able to do this:

```bash
deadreckon start "Add password reset"
```

DeadReckon would:

1. Create the isolated workspace.
2. Prepare and approve the definition of done.
3. Record a durable job.
4. Return a run ID immediately.
5. Let a background supervisor carry on.

```text
Started run dr-4821
Workspace: isolated
Status: running
Attach: deadreckon attach dr-4821
```

The terminal is no longer responsible for keeping the work alive.

```text
Terminal                 DeadReckon supervisor
   │                              │
   ├── start goal ───────────────→│
   │←── run ID ───────────────────┤
   │                              ├── run coding CLI
   │                              ├── save evidence
   │                              ├── run gate
   │                              ├── retry if appropriate
   │                              └── finish or stop explicitly
   │
   └── may close safely
```

`attach` would only observe or interact with the job. Disconnecting would not stop it.

## What keeps it durable

The background supervisor needs four basic mechanisms.

### A durable queue

`start` writes the goal into a local queue before execution begins:

```text
Job: dr-4821
Goal: Add password reset
Contract: acceptance.yaml
State: queued
Budget: $20
Deadline: 4 hours
Workspace: /path/to/worktree
```

If no supervisor is currently running, DeadReckon starts one.

### Leases and heartbeats

When a supervisor takes a job, it records:

```text
dr-4821 is leased by process 9312 until 14:35:00
```

It renews that lease periodically.

If the process crashes, the lease expires. Another supervisor can safely adopt the job. This prevents both abandonment and two supervisors working the same job simultaneously.

The uncommitted plan changes currently in the repository are moving towards this kind of orphan adoption, but it should become a shared facility for every execution shape.

### Checkpoints after every important event

DeadReckon already persists much of this. The durable executor would formalize events such as:

```text
Job started
Turn 1 started
Turn 1 completed
Gate failed
Corrective turn requested
Turn 2 completed
Gate passed
Semantic judge passed
Run verified
```

After a crash, the replacement supervisor reads this history and knows what to do next. It does not start the entire job again.

### Explicit stopping reasons

“Keep running until done” should not mean infinite retries.

A job may stop because it is:

```text
VERIFIED
BLOCKED — requires user decision
BUDGET_EXHAUSTED
DEADLINE_REACHED
FAILED — unrecoverable error
CANCELLED
```

Those states are part of the confidence model. Quietly dying because a terminal closed is not.

## It does not require a large distributed system

This could initially be a small local service:

```text
deadreckond
```

On macOS it could run through `launchd`; Linux could use a user-level `systemd` service. DeadReckon could also begin with a simpler detached conductor process, provided it has leases and automatic adoption.

It does not need Kubernetes, a server database or a cloud account. SQLite or an append-only local event log would be sufficient.

## Why this is the highest-priority gap

The original promise is not primarily “we save excellent records.” It is:

> Give the system a goal and trust it to carry responsibility for reaching a verified conclusion.

Without a durable executor, the human still carries part of that responsibility:

- keeping the process alive;
- noticing that it stopped;
- deciding whether to resume;
- restarting orchestration after a crash.

With it, the human only intervenes when DeadReckon produces an intentional `BLOCKED` state.

A practical definition of done for this feature would include:

- Start a run and close the terminal: it continues.
- Kill the coding CLI: DeadReckon retries or records a clear failure.
- Kill the supervisor: another supervisor adopts the run.
- Restart the computer: unfinished jobs resume automatically.
- Never run the same turn twice concurrently.
- Respect spend, time and retry limits.
- Preserve the same run ID, workspace and evidence throughout.
- Finish only through the normal verification boundary.

That change would turn DeadReckon from a well-persisted foreground runner into the “start it and trust it” product described in the original goal.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 22:14:26Z)**_

DeadReckon now has a credible first Watchkeeper implementation. It is substantially closer to the product promise, but the full claim still needs real-world dogfooding and reboot testing.

### What works now

- `start` creates a durable Job, returns its ID and detaches.
- An append-only event history is the lifecycle source of truth.
- Fenced leases support abandoned-work recovery without changing Job identity.
- Runs stop with explicit reasons: blocked, cancelled, budget exhausted, retries exhausted, failed or needs review.
- Single, Graph and Campaign guided starts use the shared Job supervisor.
- Completion requires both:
  1. native deterministic checks;
  2. a fresh, read-only semantic judge.
- Failed deterministic checks never reach the semantic judge.
- Unavailable or uncertain judging fails closed as `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- HMAC-authenticated receipts bind the approved goal, contract, policy, source and result.
- Gate keys remain outside agent-visible workspaces.
- `status`, `attach`, `report` and `finish` understand Jobs.
- Applying a verified result records an idempotent delivery event.
- Supervisor service commands are available for machine-restart recovery.

A live Single-job trial demonstrated detached start, isolated execution, deterministic verification, semantic achievement, receipt validation and successful delivery. The complete `make verify` gate also passed.

### Self-assessment

The necessary complexity is now concentrated around:

- immutable approved authority;
- append-only lifecycle events;
- fenced leases and process supervision;
- bounded policies and explicit outcomes;
- isolation;
- deterministic plus semantic verification;
- authenticated receipts;
- crash-safe parent recovery.

The remaining incidental complexity is mostly the older overlapping machinery:

- legacy Run, Plan, Chain and Campaign state paths;
- direct commands that do not yet use the Job scheduler;
- multiple narration and learning surfaces;
- deep Campaign behavior;
- auto-continuation variants.

Those should be consolidated or frozen, not expanded.

### What remains before making the full promise

- Execute the 24-task dogfood matrix; every row is deliberately still marked `not_run`.
- Test actual machine reboot recovery with an installed supervisor service.
- Run live Graph and Campaign trials, not only fixture and recovery tests.
- Kill terminals, workers and networks during trials and attempt receipt forgery.
- Move direct `run`, `orchestrate`, `chain` and `campaign` paths onto Jobs.
- Design safe parent repair. Graph and Campaign semantic `revise` currently stop at `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- Add aggregate Campaign time and resource accounting.
- Fix the minor post-delivery UX gap where status remains verified and may still recommend `finish`, although delivery is recorded in history.

So the honest current promise is:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. Guided Single, Graph and Campaign work can run as durable isolated Jobs, stop for bounded reasons, verify checks and meaning independently, and produce an authenticated receipt. Process recovery is implemented; full machine-restart and field reliability remain to be proven.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 22:14:26Z)**_

We have moved from architecture into a working, integrated implementation. The core mechanism is largely built; the remaining gap is proving it under sustained real-world use.

### What now works

- `start` creates a durable local job, returns its ID, and detaches.
- Jobs retain their workspace, budget, attempt history and lifecycle across worker or supervisor interruption.
- Runs, plans, chains and campaigns now converge on the same durable scheduler.
- Terminal outcomes distinguish blocked, cancelled, failed, budget exhausted, retry exhausted and needs review.
- Deterministic checks must pass before completion.
- An independent semantic judge then assesses whether the result actually satisfies the goal.
- If semantic judgment is unavailable in strict mode, the job becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`—never falsely accepted.
- Completion receipts use HMAC-SHA-256, bind the contract, policy and revisions, and detect later mutation.
- Signing material and proof paths are kept outside the agent-visible workspace.
- Provider errors are classified so fatal failures stop immediately while transient failures receive bounded retries.
- Result application/export is tracked separately from whether the work was verified.

The operator contract is documented in [WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md).

### Evidence so far

- Full `make verify`: passed.
- Release build and strict clippy: passed without warnings.
- Credential-free adversarial trials: **7 passed, 0 failed**.
- Those trials cover terminal detachment, killed workers, supervisor restart, network denial, gate-key attacks, receipt mutation and result delivery.
- Existing suites include 179 orchestration tests, 125 Chain tests and extensive Job, gate, receipt, provider and fault-matrix coverage.

### What is not proven yet

The central promise is not yet fully validated in live operation:

- Only 2 of the planned 24 live-provider tasks have been attempted.
- Neither live attempt reached verified completion.
- We have not yet performed a real machine-reboot recovery.
- Live provider interruption and restoration still need testing.
- A genuine cross-provider hostile gate attack remains untested.
- We have not completed the planned 20–30-task dogfood programme.
- A human operator has not yet run the acceptance checklist end to end.

So my honest assessment is:

> The necessary machinery exists and is strongly tested. We have not yet earned confidence in the complete product promise through live dogfooding.

+#[test]
+fn concurrent_same_goal_start_json_returns_each_exact_job_id() {
+    let temp = repo_tempdir();
+    let repo = clean_git_repo(&temp);
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+    write_start_ready_setup(&paths, &repo);
+    let goal = "concurrent exact job identity";
+
+    let mut launch = || {
+        let mut command = deadreckon(&paths);
+        command
+            .current_dir(&repo)
+            .env("DEADRECKON_TEST_START_ENVELOPE_DELAY_MS", "500")
+            .args([
+                "start", goal, "--mode", "run", "--fresh", "--yes", "--json",
+            ])
+            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
+            .stderr(Stdio::piped());
+        command.spawn().expect("spawn concurrent start")
+    };
+    let first = launch();
+    let second = launch();
+    let outputs = [
+        first.wait_with_output().expect("first start"),
+        second.wait_with_output().expect("second start"),
+    ];
+
+    let mut returned = BTreeSet::new();
+    for output in outputs {
+        assert_success(&output);
+        let envelope: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout)
+            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("start output must be JSON: {error}"));
+        let ids = envelope["dispatched"]["ids"]
+            .as_array()
+            .expect("dispatched ids");
+        assert_eq!(ids.len(), 1, "{envelope}");
+        returned.insert(ids[0].as_str().expect("job id").to_string());
+    }
+
+    assert_eq!(returned.len(), 2, "each launch must return its own Job ID");
+    assert_eq!(
+        returned,
+        job_ids(&paths),
+        "returned identities must be the exact persisted Jobs"

use super::super::*;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum StartSelectedMode {
    Extend,
    Run,
    Review,
    FullPlan,
    Campaign,
}

impl StartSelectedMode {
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Extend => "extend",
            Self::Run => "run",
            Self::Review => "review",
            Self::FullPlan => "full-plan",
            Self::Campaign => "campaign",
        }
    }

    fn path_label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Extend => "follow-up run",
            Self::Run => "run",
            Self::Review => "review orchestration",
            Self::FullPlan => "full-plan orchestration",
            Self::Campaign => "campaign orchestration",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum StartSelectionSource {
    ExplicitFlag,
    GoalShape,
    // `Heuristic` is gone: it existed only for the keyword matcher that used
    // to choose the shape before any classifier ran.
    InteractiveChoice,
    Default,
}

impl StartSelectionSource {
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ExplicitFlag => "explicit_flag",
            Self::GoalShape => "goal_shape",
            Self::InteractiveChoice => "interactive_choice",
            Self::Default => "default",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub(crate) enum GoalShape {
    Single,
    Orchestrate,
    Campaign,
}

impl GoalShape {
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Single => "single",
            Self::Orchestrate => "orchestrate",
            Self::Campaign => "campaign",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub(crate) enum GoalShapeSource {
    Provider,
    Fallback,
}

impl GoalShapeSource {
    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Provider => "provider",
            Self::Fallback => "fallback",
        }
    }
}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 22:31:22Z)**_

Overall assessment: the durable execution core is substantially built and well tested, but the full Watchkeeper promise is not yet demonstrated in real use.

What is working:

- Durable Jobs with append-only lifecycle events.
- Lease recovery, fencing, bounded retry, spend/time limits, and typed stop reasons.
- Durable Single, Graph, stored-plan, orchestration, and campaign roots.
- Deterministic checks plus a read-only semantic judge.
- HMAC receipts, gate isolation, tamper detection, and separate lifecycle/evidence stores.
- Operator commands and Job views.
- Supervisor service generation and simulated restart recovery.

What remains incomplete or unproven:

- Dogfooding is the largest gap: 24 planned trials, only 2 attempted, 22 not run, and 0 verified completions.
- Real worker termination, supervisor restart, network loss, machine reboot, and hostile cross-provider gate attacks remain unproven.
- The semantic judge can currently return `achieved` without evidence coverage; evidence-backed reasoning is not structurally required.
- Historical chain features such as hooks, apply/on-fail behavior, circuit breakers, sandbox policy, and base policy are refused rather than preserved through the Job adapter.
- Crash-before-link recovery fails safely, but does not provide exactly-once containment recovery.
- Fault injection does not yet cover every named lifecycle boundary.
- Human comprehension time, false acceptance/rejection, intervention rate, and judging cost have not been measured.
- Some committed documentation was stale relative to the implementation, although concurrent documentation work appears to be correcting that.

The necessary complexity is the Job protocol, event history, lease/fencing rules, isolated workspaces, two-key verification, protected receipts, and bounded stop policies. The incidental complexity is primarily the remaining parallel legacy lifecycle vocabulary, incomplete chain compatibility, duplicated/stale narratives, and proof infrastructure that exists without completed trials.

I also fixed the exact-ID concurrency defect. Start dispatch now returns the created Job identity directly; JSON launch no longer reconstructs identity by scanning the filesystem. See [start.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/start.rs:2795) and the concurrent same-goal regression in [orchestrate.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/tests/orchestrate.rs:7481).

Verification passed:

- New concurrent same-goal exact-ID test.
- Existing JSON launch-envelope test.
- Existing Graph Job dispatch test.
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- Focused Clippy with warnings denied.

These changes are currently uncommitted in the shared working tree for the parent agent to integrate with the other concurrent work.

---
name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive Watchkeeper dogfood metrics from persisted factual artifacts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import collections
import datetime
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


def read_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        value = json.load(handle)
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path} did not contain a JSON object")
    return value


def read_events(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
    events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    invalid = 0
    if not path.is_file():
        return events, invalid
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for raw in handle:
            if not raw.strip():
                continue
            try:
                value = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                invalid += 1
                continue
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                events.append(value)
            else:
                invalid += 1
    return events, invalid


def ratio(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> float | None:
    return round(numerator / denominator, 6) if denominator else None


def event_count(events: list[dict[str, Any]], kind: str) -> int:
    return sum(event.get("kind") == kind for event in events)


def elapsed_seconds(events: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> float | None:
    timestamps: list[datetime.datetime] = []
    for event in events:
        value = event.get("timestamp")
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            continue
        try:
            timestamps.append(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    if len(timestamps) < 2:
        return None
    return max(0.0, (max(timestamps) - min(timestamps)).total_seconds())


def semantic_spend(attempts: list[dict[str, Any]], missing: list[str]) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    seen: set[Path] = set()
    for attempt in attempts:
        marker = attempt.get("proof", {}).get("marker_path")
        if not isinstance(marker, str):
            continue
        judgment_path = Path(marker).parent / "semantic-judgment.json"
        if judgment_path in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(judgment_path)
        if not judgment_path.is_file():
            missing.append(str(judgment_path))
            continue
        judgment = read_json(judgment_path)
        total += float(judgment.get("spend_usd", 0.0))
    return total


def load_review(observation_dir: Path, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    path = observation_dir / "human-review.json"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    review = read_json(path)
    if review.get("job_id") != job_id:
        raise ValueError(f"{path} belongs to a different job")
    return review

use super::super::*;

pub(crate) struct ReportCommandArgs {
    pub(crate) run_id: String,
    pub(crate) html: bool,
    pub(crate) dest: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub(crate) open: bool,
    pub(crate) json: bool,
    pub(crate) plain: bool,
}

pub(crate) fn report_command(args: ReportCommandArgs) -> Result<()> {
    let _ = args.plain;
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    // A report renders one run's evidence, so plans and chains redirect rather
    // than coming back as "run <id> not found" for an id that plainly exists.
    let resolved = super::reference::resolve_ref(
        &paths,
        super::reference::RefQuery {
            reference: Some(&args.run_id),
            all_scopes: false,
            verb: "report",
        },
    )?;
    let state = match resolved {
        super::reference::ResolvedRef::Job(view) => {
            return report_job_command(&paths, &view, args);
        }
        super::reference::ResolvedRef::Run(state) => *state,
        super::reference::ResolvedRef::PlanChild { state, .. } => *state,
        other => {
            return Err(super::reference::refusal_for(
                other.kind(),
                "report",
                &super::reference::resolved_id(&other),
            ));
        }
    };
    if matches!(
        state.status,
        RunStatus::Pending | RunStatus::Planned | RunStatus::Executing
    ) {
        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
            &format!("run {} still running", run_prefix(&state.run_id)),
            &format!("deadreckon attach {}", run_prefix(&state.run_id)),
        )));
    }
    let view = deadreckon_core::RunView::from_state(&state)?;
    if args.json {
        println!("{}", render_report_json(&view)?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let dest = args.dest.unwrap_or_else(|| {
        state.run_root.join(if args.html {
            "report.html"
        } else {
            "report.md"
        })
    });
    if let Some(parent) = dest.parent() {
        fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    let rendered = if args.html {
        render_report_html(&view)
    } else {
        render_report_markdown(&view)
    };
    fs::write(&dest, rendered)?;
    if args.open {
        if !io::stdout().is_terminal() {
            return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
                "report --open requires an interactive terminal",
                &format!(
                    "deadreckon report {} --dest {}",
                    run_prefix(&state.run_id),
                    dest.display()
                ),
            )));
        }
        open_path(&dest)?;
    }
    print!(
        "{}",
        report_surface(&view, &dest).render_plain(!crate::completion_hints_enabled(false))
    );
    Ok(())
}

The trust gap is localized. `run.sh` currently validates only self-declared JSON fields in `receipt.json`; `collect-metrics.py` repeats the same mistake by counting a verified JobView plus `outcome/proof_kind` fields from that raw receipt. DeadReckon already exposes the correct authority in `report <job> --json`, whose receipt status comes from the core signature/digest validator, while `finish` independently validates before delivery. I’ll make the harness capture that public report, make metrics require a valid report plus a successful finish record, and prove a forged raw receipt remains at zero verified jobs.

+def report_proves_verified_completion(

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Adversarial tests for Watchkeeper's verified completion metrics."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+
+SCRIPT = Path(__file__).with_name("collect-metrics.py")
+
+
+def write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+class VerifiedCompletionMetricsTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def collect(
+        self, *, report_status: str, finish_succeeded: bool
+    ) -> dict[str, object]:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as raw_root:
+            root = Path(raw_root)
+            home = root / "home"
+            observation = root / "observations" / "task-forged" / "job-forged"
+            job_dir = home / "jobs" / "job-forged"
+
+            write_json(
+                observation / "job-view.json",
+                {
+                    "kind": "job_status",
+                    "job": {
+                        "job": {"job_id": "job-forged"},
+                        "projection": {
+                            "phase": "terminal",
+                            "outcome": "verified",
+                            "stop_reason": "verified",
+                        },
+                        "attempts": [],
+                    },
+                },
+            )
+            write_json(
+                job_dir / "receipt.json",
+                {
+                    "job_id": "job-forged",
+                    "outcome": "verified",
+                    "proof_kind": "two_key_completion",
+                    "contained": True,
+                    "sandbox_backend": "sandbox-exec",
+                    "signature": "forged-self-claim",
+                },
+            )
+            write_json(
+                observation / "job-report.json",
+                {
+                    "id": "job-forged",
+                    "phase": "terminal",
+                    "outcome": "verified",
+                    "stop_reason": "verified",
+                    "receipt": {
+                        "status": report_status,
+                        "contained": True,
+                        "sandbox_backend": "sandbox-exec",
+                        "signature_validation_error": (
+                            None if report_status == "valid" else "signature mismatch"
+                        ),
+                        "receipt": {
+                            "job_id": "job-forged",
+                            "proof_kind": "two_key_completion",
+                        },
+                    },
+                },
+            )
+            finish_status = 0 if finish_succeeded else 1
+            write_json(
+                observation / "operator-run.json",
+                {
+                    "job_id": "job-forged",
+                    "public_commands": ["start", "status", "report", "finish"],
+                    "report_attempted": True,
+                    "report_exit_status": 0,
+                    "receipt_validation_attempted": True,
+                    "receipt_validation_exit_status": (
+                        0 if report_status == "valid" else 1
+                    ),
+                    "receipt_validated": report_status == "valid",
+                    "finish_attempted": True,
+                    "finish_exit_status": finish_status,
+                    "finish_succeeded": finish_succeeded,
+                },
+            )
+
+            completed = subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    sys.executable,
+                    str(SCRIPT),
+                    "--home",
+                    str(home),
+                    "--observations",
+                    str(root / "observations"),
+                ],
+                check=True,
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+            )
+            return json.loads(completed.stdout)
+
+    def test_forged_raw_receipt_cannot_inflate_verified_jobs(self) -> None:
+        metrics = self.collect(report_status="invalid", finish_succeeded=True)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["persisted_facts"]["verified_jobs"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            metrics["persisted_facts"]["unattended_verified_jobs"], 0
+        )
+
+    def test_validation_without_successful_finish_is_not_verified(self) -> None:
+        metrics = self.collect(report_status="valid", finish_succeeded=False)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["persisted_facts"]["verified_jobs"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            metrics["persisted_facts"]["unattended_verified_jobs"], 0
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

---
name: review-against-the-working-sibling
description: Use when implementing or reviewing a feature or fix in a codebase that already contains a similar working capability — locate the known-good in-repo sibling, diff against it, and propose the minimal change to reach parity, naming the one intentional difference.
---

# Review Against the Working Sibling

Do not design behavior from scratch or judge it against abstract quality when a proven analog already exists in the repo. Find the closest working sibling, treat it as the spec, and make the new code match that pattern — calling out the single intended delta so the diff surface stays minimal.

## Steps

1. Before building or reviewing, ask "how do we already do this here?" and locate the closest working sibling — the existing button, handler, event, provider, route, or component that does the analogous job correctly.
2. Read the sibling and extract its pattern: structure, naming, where responsibility lives, how it wires up.
3. Frame the work as "make this match that, with one named difference." State the single intended delta explicitly (e.g. "same as the Save flow, but Publish instead of Preview at the end").
4. Diff the new/broken code against the sibling and propose the minimal change that restores pattern parity — not a freeform rewrite.
5. In review, make conformance the first question: "does this match the precedent?" Name the specific reference file/feature the new work must conform to.
6. If you must abandon an approach, pair the retreat with the constructive replacement — usually an already-working shape to mirror, never a speculative do-over.

## Verification

The change is right when it is structurally indistinguishable from its named sibling except for the one stated delta. If you cannot name the sibling and the delta, you have not grounded the work.

## Failure modes

- Inventing a fresh implementation when a working analog exists — it drifts from house conventions and is harder to review.
- Reviewing for abstract "quality" instead of "does it match how we already do it?".
- Carrying over template/sibling code without adapting the one part that must differ (the user catches lines that are "not sufficiently adapted").

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-05). Consolidates anchor-review-in-working-sibling, precedent-conformance-check, and abandon-only-toward-a-working-exemplar.

//! Durable job creation and detached supervisor launch.
//!
//! `start` resolves and approves the mutable inputs. This module freezes those
//! inputs before the first agent turn, writes the initial append-only control
//! facts, and only then starts a supervisor.

use super::super::*;

use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

use chrono::Utc;
use deadreckon_protocol::{
    AuthorityAcceptedBy, Job, JobAuthority, JobEvent, JobEventKind, JobEventSequence, JobId,
    JobPolicy, JobSchemaVersion, JobShape, RunId, SemanticJudgeMode, StopReason,
};

const JOB_ACCEPTANCE_FILE: &str = "acceptance.yaml";
const SUPERVISOR_LAUNCH_STDOUT: &str = "supervisor.out";
const SUPERVISOR_LAUNCH_STDERR: &str = "supervisor.err";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub(crate) enum DurableSourceMode {
    Worktree,
    Copy,
    Fresh,
    InitGit,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct DurableSource {
    pub(crate) mode: DurableSourceMode,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub(crate) from: Option<PathBuf>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) allow_dirty: bool,
}

pub(crate) struct CreateJob<'a> {
    pub(crate) paths: &'a DeadreckonPaths,
    pub(crate) source_cwd: &'a Path,
    pub(crate) scope: String,
    pub(crate) launch_plan: commands::course::LaunchPlan,
    pub(crate) shape: JobShape,
    pub(crate) driver: Option<commands::graph_job::DriverSpec>,
    pub(crate) contract_source: Option<&'a Path>,
    pub(crate) source: DurableSource,
    pub(crate) max_spend_usd: f64,
    pub(crate) max_wall_seconds: u64,
    pub(crate) max_attempts: u32,
    pub(crate) sandbox_requested: String,
    pub(crate) accepted_by: AuthorityAcceptedBy,
}

pub(crate) fn create_job(mut request: CreateJob<'_>) -> Result<Job> {
    let expected_shape = match request.launch_plan.shape {
        commands::course::CourseShape::Single => JobShape::Single,
        commands::course::CourseShape::Plan => JobShape::Graph,
        commands::course::CourseShape::Campaign => JobShape::LegacyCampaign,
        commands::course::CourseShape::ChainExtend => {
            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
                "legacy chain jobs remain process-bound; direct chain execution must compile to a durable linear graph".to_string(),
            )));
        }
    };
    if request.shape != expected_shape {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "durable job shape does not match its launch plan".to_string(),
        )));
    }
    if let Some(driver) = request.driver.as_ref() {
        commands::graph_job::embed_driver_spec(&mut request.launch_plan, driver)?;
    } else if request.shape != JobShape::Single {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
            "advanced durable jobs require an immutable driver specification".to_string(),
        )));
    }
    let job_id = JobId(Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string());
    let job_dir = request.paths.job_dir(job_id.as_ref());
    fs::create_dir_all(&job_dir)?;
    let authority_source_cwd =

    let mut signals = request
        .launch_plan
        .signals
        .as_object()
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_default();
    signals.insert(
        "watchkeeper_source".to_string(),
        serde_json::to_value(&request.source)?,
    );
    request.launch_plan.signals = serde_json::Value::Object(signals);

    let launch_path = request.paths.job_launch_plan(job_id.as_ref());
    commands::course::save_launch_plan(&launch_path, &request.launch_plan)?;
    sync_file(&launch_path)?;
    let launch_plan_sha256 = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&launch_path)?;

    let contract_path = job_dir.join(JOB_ACCEPTANCE_FILE);
    freeze_contract(
        request.contract_source,
        &authority_source_cwd,
        &contract_path,
    )?;
    let contract_sha256 = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&contract_path)?;

    let policy = JobPolicy {
        max_spend_usd: request.max_spend_usd,
        max_wall_seconds: request.max_wall_seconds,
        max_attempts: request.max_attempts.max(1),
        deadline: None,
        semantic_judge: SemanticJudgeMode::Required,

    let effective_policy_sha256 = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(

        })?,
    );
    let source_tree_sha256 =

    let authority = JobAuthority {
        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
        job_id: job_id.clone(),
        run_id: RunId(job_id.as_ref().to_string()),
        approved_at: Utc:

fn direct_run_approval_policy(
    yes: bool,
    no_confirm: bool,
    _quiet: bool,
    is_tty: bool,
    goal: &str,
    no_hints: bool,
) -> Result<bool> {
    if yes || no_confirm {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if !is_tty {
        return Err(durable_run_confirmation_refusal_error(goal, no_hints));
    }
    Ok(false)
}

fn direct_run_source(cwd: &Path, args: &RunCommandArgs) -> Result<commands::job::DurableSource> {
    let (mode, from) = if args.fresh {
        (commands::job::DurableSourceMode::Fresh, None)
    } else if let Some(from) = args.from.as_ref() {
        (
            commands::job::DurableSourceMode::Copy,
            Some(resolve_direct_source_path(cwd, from)),
        )
    } else if args.init_git || args.worktree || deadreckon_core::find_git_root(cwd)?.is_some() {
        (commands::job::DurableSourceMode::Worktree, None)
    } else {
        (
            commands::job::DurableSourceMode::Copy,
            Some(cwd.to_path_buf()),
        )
    };
    Ok(commands::job::DurableSource {
        mode,
        from,
        allow_dirty: args.allow_dirty,
    })
}

fn resolve_direct_source_path(cwd: &Path, requested: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    if requested.is_absolute() {
        requested.to_path_buf()
    } else {
        cwd.join(requested)
    }
}

pub(crate) fn strip_code_fence(value: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = value.trim();
    if !trimmed.starts_with("```") {
        return trimmed.to_string();
    }
    let mut lines = trimmed.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if lines.len() >= 2 && lines.last().is_some_and(|line| line.trim() == "```") {
        lines.remove(0);
        lines.pop();
        return lines.join("\n");
    }
    trimmed.to_string()
}

fn extract_json_object(value: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let start = value.find('{')?;
    let end = value.rfind('}')?;
    if end <= start {
        return None;
    }
    Some(value[start..=end].to_string())
}

pub(crate) fn extract_fenced_block(value: &str, languages: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    let mut in_block = false;
    let mut capture = false;
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    for line in value.lines() {
        let trimmed = line.trim();
        if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_prefix("```") {
            if in_block {
                if capture {
                    return Some(lines.join("\n"));
                }
                in_block = false;
                continue;
            }
            in_block = true;
            capture = languages
                .iter()
                .any(|language| rest.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(language));
            lines.clear();
            continue;
        }
        if in_block && capture {
            lines.push(line);
        }
    }
    None
}

pub(crate) async fn ensure_acceptance_before_start(
    cwd: &Path,
    override_path: Option<&Path>,
    goal: &str,
    provider: Option<String>,
    model: Option<String>,
    skip_prompt: bool,
    noun: &str,
) -> Result<Option<AcceptanceSource>> {
    let existing = resolve_acceptance_source(cwd, override_path)?;
    if existing.is_some() || override_path.is_some() || skip_prompt || !io::stdin().is_terminal() {
        return Ok(existing);
    }
    println!("{}", ui_heading("done criteria"));
    println!("No done criteria found.");
    println!("Write the definition of done in English; deadreckon will compile it for dr-gate.");
    if !prompt::confirm(&format!("write done criteria before this {noun}?"), true)? {
        println!("using default gate: working directory exists, or cargo test for Rust projects");
        return Ok(existing);
    }
    let request = prompt::open("definition of done (Enter for a practical default): ", None)?;
    let request = if request.trim().is_empty() {
        format!("For this {noun}, define practical acceptance checks for: {goal}")
    } else {
        request.trim().to_string()
    };
    match acceptance_agent_command_in_dir(
        cwd,
        AcceptanceAgentMode::Draft,
        vec![request],
        Some(goal),
        provider,
        model,
        false,
    )
    .await
    {
        Ok(()) => resolve_acceptance_source(cwd, None).map(mark_generated_done_criteria),
        Err(err) => {
            println!("{}", ui_status("done criteria draft failed"));
            println!("  {err}");
            if !prompt::confirm("use a detected local check template instead?", true)? {
                return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
                    "done criteria were requested but not configured",
                    "rerun `deadreckon def-done \"what should count as done\"` or answer yes to the detected template fallback",
                )));
            }
            let preset = detect_acceptance_preset(cwd);
            let draft = acceptance_template_for_preset(preset, cwd);
            write_project_acceptance(cwd, &draft, false, false)?;
            print_acceptance_written(
                cwd,
                "detected template",
                acceptance_check_count(&draft.yaml)?,
            );
            resolve_acceptance_source(cwd, None).map(mark_generated_done_criteria)
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_acceptance_source(
    cwd: &Path,
    override_path: Option<&Path>,
) -> Result<Option<AcceptanceSource>> {
    if let Some(path) = override_path {
        let path = absolute_from(cwd, path);
        if !path.is_file() {
            return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
                &format!("done criteria file not found: {}", path.display()),
                "deadreckon def-done \"what should count as done\"",
            )));
        }
        return Ok(Some(AcceptanceSource {
            path,
            source: setup::DoneCriteriaSource::ExplicitPath,
            companion_doc: None,
        }));
    }
    let project_yaml = project_acceptance_yaml(cwd);
    if project_yaml.is_file() {
        let project_md = project_acceptance_md(cwd);
        return Ok(Some(AcceptanceSource {
            path: project_yaml,
            source: setup::DoneCriteriaSource::ProjectFile,
            companion_doc: project_md.is_file().then_some(project_md),
        }));

    provider: &str,
    plain: bool,
    signals: &commands::course::SignalBundle,
    ladder: &commands::course::LadderDecision,
) -> Option<commands::course::ResolvedCoursePlan> {
    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path(&paths.config_path(), Some(provider)).ok()?;
    let request = ProviderRequest {
        prompt: commands::course::course_planner_prompt(goal, signals),
        max_output_tokens: 512,
        cwd: Some(cwd.to_path_buf()),
        output_path: None,
        sandbox_backend: None,
        workspace_access: deadreckon_providers::WorkspaceAccess::ReadWrite,
        pid_file: None,
        cancellation_token: None,
        session_dir: None,
        output_schema: None,
        capability_posture: None,
    };
    let response = tokio::time::timeout(
        course_planner_timeout(provider),
        maybe_with_cli_wait_status(!plain, "plotting the course", router.complete(&request)),
    )
    .await
    .ok()?
    .ok()?;
    commands::course::resolve_provider_course_plan(
        &response.content,
        signals,
        ladder,
        commands::course::SHAPE_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR_DEFAULT,
    )
}

/// CLI subagent providers cold-start in ~10-15s; the 5s ceiling that suits
/// HTTP routes guarantees a silent ladder fallback for them. The planner is
/// one bounded read-only call either way — give CLIs room to answer.
pub(crate) fn course_planner_timeout(provider: &str) -> Duration {
    if provider.starts_with("cli:") {
        Duration::from_secs(30)
    } else {
        Duration::from_secs(5)
    }
}

fn course_shape_to_goal_shape(shape: commands::course::CourseShape) -> GoalShape {
    match shape {
        // Chain-extend rides the single-run recommendation until dispatch
        // consumes the plan file directly (C-P9); the rationale carries the
        // continuation story.
        commands::course::CourseShape::Single | commands::course::CourseShape::ChainExtend => {
            GoalShape::Single
        }
        commands::course::CourseShape::Plan => GoalShape::Orchestrate,
        commands::course::CourseShape::Campaign => GoalShape::Campaign,
    }
}

/// Convert a ladder decision into the recommendation shape the preview and
/// campaign seeding consume — the provider-free classification floor.
/// Campaign is never a deterministic outcome (Course doctrine: deterministic
/// campaign selection is a spend hazard).
pub(crate) fn ladder_goal_shape_recommendation(
    goal: &str,
    ladder: &commands::course::LadderDecision,
) -> GoalShapeRecommendation {
    let resolution = commands::course::ladder_resolution(ladder);
    GoalShapeRecommendation {
        schema_version: 1,
        goal: goal.to_string(),
        shape: course_shape_to_goal_shape(ladder.shape),
        n: ladder.n,
        rationale: resolution.rationale,
        source: GoalShapeSource::Fallback,
        provider: None,
        // The ladder decides shape and n from measured signals; it does not
        // author node goals, so plan creation falls back to its own planner.
        pieces: Vec::new(),
        // The ladder does ask for incremental landing, but only when the goal
        // spells out an order ("migrate, then update, then delete"). Ordering
        // is a structural fact in the text, not a spend gamble — and it is the
        // one shape `start` previously could not reach at all.
        apply: ladder.apply,
    }
}

fn goal_shape_to_start_mode(shape: GoalShape) -> StartSelectedMode {
    match shape {
        GoalShape::Single => StartSelectedMode::Run,
        GoalShape::Orchestrate => StartSelectedMode::FullPlan,
        GoalShape::Campaign => StartSelectedMode::Campaign,
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ModeFlags {
    pub fresh: bool,
    pub worktree: bool,
    pub from: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub in_place: bool,
    pub i_know_its_a_lot: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct WorktreeOptions {
    pub run_id: String,
    pub task_key: String,
    pub source_path: PathBuf,
    pub base_ref: Option<String>,
    pub branch_name: Option<String>,
    pub allow_dirty: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PreviewGitState {
    pub git_root: PathBuf,
    pub branch: String,
    pub head_sha: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ResolvedMode {
    Worktree {
        source_path: PathBuf,
        git_root: PathBuf,
    },
    Copy {
        source_path: PathBuf,
    },
    InPlace {
        source_path: PathBuf,
    },
    Fresh,
}

impl ResolvedMode {
    pub fn mode(&self) -> CodebaseMode {
        match self {
            Self::Worktree { .. } => CodebaseMode::Worktree,
            Self::Copy { .. } => CodebaseMode::Copy,
            Self::InPlace { .. } => CodebaseMode::InPlace,
            Self::Fresh => CodebaseMode::Fresh,
        }
    }
}

pub fn resolve_mode(flags: &ModeFlags, cwd: &Path, tty: bool) -> Result<ResolvedMode> {
    if flags.fresh {
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Fresh);
    }
    if flags.in_place {
        if !flags.i_know_its_a_lot && !tty {
            return Err(user_error(
                "--in-place requires --i-know-its-a-lot or interactive confirm",
                "add --i-know-its-a-lot or run in a TTY",
            ));
        }
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::InPlace {
            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
        });
    }
    if let Some(source_path) = flags.from.as_ref() {
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Copy {
            source_path: canonical_or_self(source_path)?,
        });
    }
    if flags.worktree {
        let git_root = find_git_root(cwd)?.ok_or_else(|| {
            user_error(
                &format!("{} is not a git repo", cwd.display()),
                "git init or pass --from .",
            )
        })?;
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Worktree {
            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
            git_root,
        });
    }
    if let Some(git_root) = find_git_root(cwd)? {
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Worktree {
            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
            git_root,
        });
    }
    if tty {
        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Copy {
            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
        });
    }
    Err(user_error(
        "non-interactive without a mode flag",
        "--fresh or --from . or git init",
    ))
}
}

pub fn record_for_resolved_mode(mode: ResolvedMode) -> CodebaseRecord {
    let mut record = CodebaseRecord::fresh();
    match mode {
        ResolvedMode::Fresh => {}
        ResolvedMode::Copy { source_path } => {
            record.mode = CodebaseMode::Copy;
            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
        }
        ResolvedMode::InPlace { source_path } => {
            record.mode = CodebaseMode::InPlace;
            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
        }
        ResolvedMode::Worktree {
            source_path,
            git_root,
        } => {
            record.mode = CodebaseMode::Worktree;
            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
            record.source_git_root = Some(git_root);
        }
    }
    record
}

fn load_launch_inputs(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> Result<LaunchInputs> {
    let plan_path = paths.job_launch_plan(job.job_id.as_ref());
    let plan_digest = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&plan_path)?;
    if plan_digest != job.launch_plan_sha256 {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "launch plan digest mismatch for job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    let plan = super::course::load_launch_plan(&plan_path)?;
    let expected_shape = match job.shape {
        JobShape::Single => CourseShape::Single,
        JobShape::Graph => CourseShape::Plan,
        JobShape::LegacyCampaign => CourseShape::Campaign,
        JobShape::LegacyChain => CourseShape::ChainExtend,
    };
    if plan.shape != expected_shape || plan.goal != job.goal {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "launch plan identity does not match job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    if job.shape != JobShape::Single {
        super::graph_job::driver_spec(&plan)?;
    }

    let authority_path = paths.job_authority(job.job_id.as_ref());
    let authority_digest = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&authority_path)?;
    if authority_digest != job.authority_sha256 {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "authority digest mismatch for job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    let authority: JobAuthority = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&authority_path)?)?;
    if authority.job_id != job.job_id
        || authority.run_id != RunId(job.job_id.as_ref().to_string())
        || authority.launch_plan_sha256 != job.launch_plan_sha256
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "authority identity does not match job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "goal",
        &authority.goal_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(&job.goal),
    )?;
    let contract_path = super::job::job_acceptance_path(paths, job.job_id.as_ref());
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "done contract",
        &authority.contract_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&contract_path)?,
    )?;
    let policy_sha256 = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_text(
        &serde_json::to_string(&job.policy).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: paths.job_json(job.job_id.as_ref()),
            source,
        })?,
    );
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "effective policy",
        &authority.effective_policy_sha256,
        &policy_sha256,
    )?;
    require_authority_digest(
        job,
        "source tree",
        &authority.source_tree_sha256,
        &deadreckon_core::flight::build_working_file_index(&job.source_cwd)?.tree_hash(),
    )?;
    if authority.semantic_judge_mode != job.policy.semantic_judge {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "semantic judge policy mismatch for job {}",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    if let Some(expected) = authority.source_revision.as_deref()
        && current_source_revision(&job.source_cwd).as_deref() != Some(expected)
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "source revision changed after job {} was approved",
            job.job_id
        ))));
    }
    Ok(LaunchInputs { plan, authority })
}

fn require_authority_digest(job: &Job, label: &str, expected: &str, actual: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if expected == actual {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "{label} changed after job {} was approved",
            job.job_id
        ))))
    }
}

fn current_source_revision(cwd: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    let output = deadreckon_core::git::run_git(cwd, &["rev-parse", "HEAD"]).ok()?;
    output
        .status
}

fn effective_spend(job: &Job, plan: &LaunchPlan) -> f64 {
    plan.budget
        .ceiling_usd
        .map_or(job.policy.max_spend_usd, |plan_cap| {
            plan_cap.min(job.policy.max_spend_usd)
        })
}

fn effective_wall_seconds(job: &Job, plan: &LaunchPlan) -> u64 {

fn child_metadata(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> Result<Option<SupervisedProcess>> {
    let path = child_metadata_path(paths, job_id);
    let metadata = match read_supervised_process(&path) {
        Ok(metadata) => metadata,
        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
        Err(source) => return Err(source.into()),
    };
    Ok(Some(metadata))
}

async fn monitor_child(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    mut child: MonitoredChild,
) -> Result<ChildExit> {
    loop {
        let status = match &mut child {
            MonitoredChild::Owned(child) => child.try_wait()?,
            MonitoredChild::Adopted(pid) if !pid_is_alive(*pid) => {
                return Ok(ChildExit {
                    status: None,
                    adopted: true,
                });
            }
            MonitoredChild::Adopted(_) => None,
        };
        if let Some(status) = status {
            return Ok(ChildExit {
                status: Some(status),
                adopted: false,
            });
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL).await;
        heartbeat_job_lease(paths, token, Utc::now(), LEASE_TTL)?;
    }
}

impl PipelineState {
    pub fn state_path(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.run_root.join("state.json")
    }

    pub fn set_phase_status(&mut self, id: PhaseId, status: PhaseStatus) -> Result<()> {
        let now = Utc::now();
        let phase = self
            .phases
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|phase| phase.id == id)
            .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("phase {}", id.0)))?;
        phase.status = status;
        phase.updated_at = now;
        self.current_phase_id = id;
        self.updated_at = now;
        self.status = match status {
            PhaseStatus::Executing => RunStatus::Executing,
            PhaseStatus::Failed => RunStatus::Failed,
            PhaseStatus::Completed if id == PhaseId(60) => RunStatus::Completed,
            PhaseStatus::Planned => RunStatus::Planned,
            PhaseStatus::Pending | PhaseStatus::Completed => self.status,
        };
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn active_phase(&self) -> Option<&PhaseState> {
        self.phases
            .iter()
            .find(|phase| phase.id == self.current_phase_id)
    }
}

fn resolve_skill_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, skill_name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let relative = Path::new("skills").join(skill_name).join("SKILL.md");
    let user = paths.home().join(&relative);
    if user.exists() {
        return user;
    }
    if let Some(root) = source_root() {
        let repo = root.join(&relative);
        if repo.exists() {
            return repo;
        }
    }
    user
}

pub fn create_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, options: RunOptions) -> Result<PipelineState> {
    let scope = workspace_scope(&options.cwd)?;
    let task_key = task_key(&options.goal);
    let run_id = options
        .run_id
        .unwrap_or_else(|| Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string());
    let run_root = paths.run_root(&scope, &run_id);
    let codebase = options.codebase.unwrap_or_else(CodebaseRecord::fresh);
    let working_dir = working_dir_for_codebase(&run_root, &codebase);
    fs::create_dir_all(&working_dir).with_path(&working_dir)?;
    fs::create_dir_all(run_root.join("snapshots")).with_path(run_root.join("snapshots"))?;
    let gate_dir = run_root.join("gate");
    fs::create_dir_all(&gate_dir).with_path(&gate_dir)?;
    create_gate_key(paths, &run_id)?;

    // AS-BUILT §3: the binary owns deterministic paths while the skill stays a
    // markdown subprocess boundary. User skills (<home>/skills) win over the
    // source checkout; a missing file falls back to the built-in contract at read
    // time, so installed binaries without either tier still run.

    let root = env::var_os("DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .or_else(|| find_git_root(start))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| start.to_path_buf());

        path: root.clone(),
        source,
    })?;

        .map(sanitize_slug)
        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())

    Ok(format!(
        "{base}-{:08x}",
        fnv1a32(canonical.to_string_lossy().as_ref())
    ))
}

/// Fold history in append order. Exact repeated event bytes are idempotent;
/// conflicting IDs, identity changes and sequence gaps are corruption.
pub fn reduce_job_history(job_id: &JobId, history: &JobHistory) -> Result<JobProjection> {
    let mut projection = JobProjection::empty(job_id.clone());
    projection.caveats.clone_from(&history.caveats);
    let mut expected = 1_u64;
    let mut seen = BTreeMap::<&str, &[u8]>::new();
    let mut child_ids = BTreeSet::new();

    for (event, raw) in history.events.iter().zip(&history.raw_lines) {
        if event.job_id != *job_id {
            return Err(history_corrupt(
                job_id.as_ref(),
                &format!("event belongs to {}", event.job_id),
            ));
        }
        if let Some(prior) = seen.get(event.event_id.as_str()) {
            if *prior == raw.as_slice() {
                continue;
            }
            return Err(history_corrupt(
                job_id.as_ref(),
                &format!("event id {} has conflicting bytes", event.event_id),
            ));
        }
        if event.sequence.get() != expected {
            return Err(history_corrupt(
                job_id.as_ref(),
                &format!(
                    "expected event sequence {expected}, found {}",
                    event.sequence.get()
                ),
            ));
        }
        seen.insert(event.event_id.as_str(), raw.as_slice());
        expected += 1;
        projection.last_sequence = event.sequence.get();
        projection.updated_at = Some(event.timestamp);
        reduce_event(&mut projection, event, &mut child_ids)?;
    }
    projection.child_run_ids = child_ids.into_iter().collect();
    Ok(projection)
}

fn maybe_schedule_leaf_retry(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    job: &Job,
    token: &LeaseToken,
    exit: &ChildExit,
    attempt: u32,
    max_attempts: u32,
) -> Result<bool> {
    if attempt >= max_attempts {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let Ok(state) = load_run(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) else {
        // Without persisted run state there is no isolated checkpoint to
        // continue safely. The caller classifies this as a terminal failure.
        return Ok(false);
    };
    let terminal_by_policy = state
        .max_spend_usd
        .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_spend_usd >= cap)
        || state
            .max_wall_seconds
            .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_wall_seconds >= cap);
    if terminal_by_policy {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let retry_stop_reason = match state.status {
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Pending
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Planned
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Executing => StopReason::LostContainment,
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed
            if state.provider_failure == Some(ProviderFailureDisposition::Retryable) =>
        {
            StopReason::TransientProvider
        }
        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Completed
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Killed
        | deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed => return Ok(false),
    };

    append_attempt_stopped(
        paths,
        token,
        retry_stop_reason,
        json!({
            "attempt": attempt,
            "exit": exit_detail(exit),
            "run_status": state.status,
            "failure_reason": state.failure_reason,
            "provider_failure": state.provider_failure,
            "reason": "worker stopped with a resumable isolated run"
        }),
    )?;
    append_control_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::RetryScheduled,
        format!("leaf-retry:{}:{attempt}", token.epoch),
        json!({
            "after_attempt": attempt,
            "reason": "resume_persisted_run"
        }),
    )?;
    reason: StopReason,
    message: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    append_attempt_stopped(
        paths,
        token,
        reason,
        json!({ "exit": exit_detail(&exit), "reason": message }),
    )?;
    append_terminal_event(
        paths,
        token,
        JobEventKind::Failed,
        reason,
        json!({ "reason": message }),
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

pub fn load_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, run_id: &str) -> Result<PipelineState> {

    load_state(&path)
}

pub fn list_runs(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, scope_filter: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<RunListEntry>> {
    let root = paths.runstate_dir();
    if !root.exists() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    let mut runs = Vec::new();
    for entry in WalkDir::new(&root)
        .max_depth(4)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
    {
        if !entry.file_type().is_file() || entry.file_name() != "state.json" {
            continue;
        }
        let state = load_state(entry.path())?;
        if scope_filter.is_some_and(|scope| scope != state.scope) {
            continue;
        }
        runs.push(RunListEntry {
            run_id: state.run_id,
            scope: state.scope,
            goal: state.goal,
            status: state.status,
            status: state.status,
            updated_at: state.updated_at,
            state_path: entry.path().to_path_buf(),
        });
    }
    runs.sort_by(|left, right| right.updated_at.cmp(&left.updated_at));
    Ok(runs)
}

pub(crate) fn atomic_write_json<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))
    })?;
    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
    let mut temp = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).with_path(parent)?;
    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut temp, value).with_json_path(path)?;
    temp.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
    temp.as_file_mut().sync_all().with_path(path)?;
    persist_temp(temp, path)
}

fn persist_temp(temp: NamedTempFile, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    match temp.persist(path) {
        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
        Err(err) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            source: err.error,
        }),
    }
}
